business_problem: Jettime relied on a massive spreadsheet for long-term crew planning, and the model could not keep up with route complexity, rule management or fluctuating flight volumes for a smaller airline.
solution_summary: Jettime partnered with IBM Business Partner CogniTech to build a workforce-forecasting model on IBM Planning Analytics. The airline needed a more accurate way to place pilots and cabin crew across complex multi-country routes while also linking the staffing outlook to financial and HR budgets. Planning Analytics became the rule-driven planning engine for crew pairings, replacing the oversized spreadsheet that had limited scalability and unreliable outputs. The implementation embedded operational logic directly into the model so controllers could run what-if scenarios, plan up to five years ahead and trust that the same forecast would not need to be rebuilt manually after each change. By turning crew planning into a governed analytics workflow instead of an Excel exercise, Jettime created a reusable planning asset that supports cost control, more predictable staffing and future extensions into fleet, maintenance and pricing simulations.

solution_components.name: IBM Planning Analytics
solution_components.role: Runs the rules-based workforce forecasting model that calculates crew pairings and long-range staffing needs.

data_flow: Flight volumes, crew rules and scheduling assumptions flow into IBM Planning Analytics, which calculates crew pairings and multi-year staffing forecasts that are then used to support financial and HR planning decisions.
business_outcome: Jettime improved confidence in its workforce forecast, reduced planning effort from days to hours and unlocked six-figure savings while building a model it can extend into other airline planning domains.
